posts.title: Helping a cat recover at home
posts.excerpt: A warm corner, a low litter tray and quiet: small things that help a cat heal after surgery.
posts.content:
Cats recover best somewhere quiet and warm, away from stairs and other pets. A cardboard box on its side with a soft towel is often all they need.

Use a low litter tray for the first few days, keep water close, and call us if your cat has not eaten within a day of coming home.

posts.title: Autumn walks and paws
posts.excerpt: Fallen leaves hide thorns and wet pavements soften pads. A short check after each walk helps.
posts.content:
After a wet walk, dry between the toes and look for small cuts or seeds caught in the fur.

Older dogs may stiffen in the cold mornings; a shorter, slower first walk of the day is kind to their joints.

posts.title: A gentle first year for puppies
posts.excerpt: Vaccines, a weigh-in and lots of handling practice: our plan for a puppy's first months.
posts.content:
Most puppies need two vaccine visits, about four weeks apart, and a booster a year later.

Between visits, practise touching paws, ears and mouth for a few seconds a day, with a treat. It makes every later check easier.

posts.title: Rabbits need hay first
posts.excerpt: Most rabbit tooth and tummy problems start with too little hay. Here is the simple rule we give.
posts.content:
A rabbit should eat a pile of hay the size of its own body every day. Pellets and greens are extras, not the main meal.

Rabbit teeth grow all their lives; chewing hay wears them down evenly. Bring your rabbit in if it drops food or stops eating.

posts.title: What happens in the waiting room
posts.excerpt: Why we keep cats and dogs apart, and how to make the wait easier for a nervous pet.
posts.content:
Our cat room has raised shelves for carriers: cats feel safer up high, away from dogs' noses.

Cover the carrier with a towel that smells of home, and speak softly. We call you in as soon as the room is ready.

posts.title: A quieter summer for older dogs
posts.excerpt: Heat is harder on older dogs. Early walks, shade and fresh water go a long way.
posts.content:
Walk before eight in the morning and after seven in the evening, when the pavement has cooled.

Watch for heavy panting or slowness, and keep a bowl of fresh water in two places at home.
